0.long_answer: Gómez–López-Hernández syndrome has been linked to mutations in the Acp2 gene. This gene is located on the short arm of human chromosome 11 (regions 11p11 to 11p12) and encodes lysosomal acid phosphatase, an enzyme that is composed of two subunits. The structure of such enzymes typically relies on the proper assembly of these subunits to be functionally active, a process that is critical for their role in normal cellular and neurological processes. Alterations in Acp2 disrupt these processes and have been implicated in the development of Gómez–López-Hernández syndrome.
